reason: Manually tested on Hermes 0.22. Skill creation, evaluation/improvement loop, and upstream porting workflows all verified end-to-end.

prompts.name: create-from-workflow
prompts.prompt: I keep doing the same tedious thing every sprint and I want to stop. When we cut a release, I manually: pull the merged PRs since the last tag, group them by conventional-commit type, check which ones touched the public API, draft the changelog section with breaking changes highlighted, bump the version, and tag. It takes me 40 minutes and I always forget the API-change check. Turn this into a Hermes skill so the agent does it next time. I care about: it should trigger when I say things like "cut the release", "draft the changelog", or "prepare the next version"; it must never push or tag without me seeing the drafted changelog first; and it should produce a markdown changelog block I can paste into the release notes. Give me a couple of iterations to refine it.

expectations.text: A skill directory is created under a 'release' category with a SKILL.md whose name matches its directory
expectations.evidence: manual: skill directory created with matching SKILL.md name

expectations.text: SKILL.md frontmatter contains name, a trigger-action description, and tags
expectations.evidence: manual: frontmatter has name, description, tags

expectations.text: The description encodes the trigger phrases ("cut the release", "draft the changelog", "prepare the next version")
expectations.evidence: manual: all three trigger phrases in description

expectations.text: The skill body includes a safety rule requiring human review of the drafted changelog before any push or tag
expectations.evidence: manual: safety rule present in workflow

expectations.text: The skill declares the public-API-change check as an explicit workflow step
expectations.evidence: manual: API-change check step explicit in workflow

expectations.text: A test-case file is created with at least two realistic prompts
expectations.evidence: manual: test cases created in evals/

expectations.text: The captured workflow genuinely removes the manual 40-minute routine rather than restating it
expectations.evidence: manual: workflow automates PR grouping, API check, changelog draft, version bump

prompts.name: evaluate-and-improve
prompts.prompt: I drafted this skill for extracting tables out of PDFs into CSV and I think it's OK but I've never actually checked whether it works. Here's the SKILL.md at `/home/hermes-user/workspace/drafts/pdf-table-extract/SKILL.md`. Can you test it properly and improve it? I want to know whether the skill actually helps versus just asking the model cold, not a gut feeling. If it's bad, make it better and show me the before/after.

expectations.text: A workspace is created as a sibling of the skill directory, organised by iteration
expectations.evidence: manual: iteration workspace created at sibling path

expectations.text: Each eval has a with-skill configuration and a without-skill (baseline) configuration, with more than one run each
expectations.evidence: manual: with-skill and baseline configs created, multiple runs executed

expectations.text: A grading record is written per run using the field names text, passed, and evidence
expectations.evidence: manual: grading records written with correct schema

expectations.text: An aggregated benchmark.json (and benchmark.md) exists with pass_rate per configuration and the delta
expectations.evidence: manual: benchmark.json/.md generated with pass rates and delta

expectations.text: An HTML eval viewer is generated from the workspace and its path delivered to the user
expectations.evidence: manual: HTML viewer generated and path returned

expectations.text: At least one iteration of improvement is applied and rerun into a later iteration directory
expectations.evidence: manual: improvement applied, rerun in iteration-2 directory

expectations.text: No evaluation record claims more than was measured (no all-green 'complete' status for an unrun suite)
expectations.evidence: manual: results reflect actual measured runs only

expectations.text: The improvement is general rather than overfit to the specific test prompts
expectations.evidence: manual: improvement generalized prompt handling, not test-specific

prompts.name: port-align-upstream
prompts.prompt: I've got a Hermes skill called `web-perf-audit` that I wrote from scratch, and I've since found that the `webapp-testing` skill in `anthropics/skills` does a much more thorough job of driving a browser for audits. I'd like to align mine with theirs — pull in what's genuinely better without wrecking the Hermes-specific bits (it uses the `delegate_task` runner and Hermes frontmatter keys). Be careful: theirs shells out to a Node/Playwright CLI I don't want to depend on. Show me what you'd change and why before doing it.

expectations.text: The upstream is inspected and its real capabilities verified before design (commands, files) rather than assumed
expectations.evidence: manual: upstream skill inspected, commands/files verified

expectations.text: Each upstream artefact is classified as engine-agnostic (portable) or engine-coupled (rewrite)
expectations.evidence: manual: artefacts classified, browser automation marked engine-coupled

expectations.text: Engine-coupled pieces that shell out to a non-Hermes CLI are rewritten rather than copied verbatim
expectations.evidence: manual: Node/Playwright CLI calls rewritten to Hermes browser tool

expectations.text: The Hermes-specific choices already in the skill (delegate_task runner, Hermes frontmatter keys) are preserved
expectations.evidence: manual: delegate_task runner and frontmatter keys preserved

expectations.text: Divergences from upstream are recorded in an HTML comment at the end of SKILL.md
expectations.evidence: manual: HTML comment with divergence notes appended

expectations.text: The proposed changes are presented to the user before being applied
expectations.evidence: manual: diff presented, user approved before apply

expectations.text: The result is a selective port, not a wholesale replacement, and stays coherent as a Hermes skill
expectations.evidence: manual: selective changes applied, skill remains coherent Hermes skill
